title: Nvidia $63 Billion Secret Portfolio and 18 Stocks I’m Watching
creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
summary: Joseph Hogue argues Nvidia's $63 billion 13F stock portfolio, $230 billion-plus of lease guarantees and $500 billion-plus financing platforms (with Apollo, BlackRock and Goldman Sachs) are not just circular-financing risk — the Wall Street Journal's Lucent comparison — but a road map to the next AI winners: follow the money and the bottlenecks Nvidia is paying to solve (optics, networking, memory, power, cooling). He ranks 18 stocks by dependence on Nvidia. Tier 1, highest dependence: CoreWeave and Nebius are his biggest question marks, Intel is a pass (foundry execution vs TSMC unproven, despite Nvidia's ~$30B stake), while Synopsys is a like — critical design software, ~37% expected revenue growth, still attractively valued. Tier 2 holds his favourite opportunities: Coherent and Lumentum on the optical bottleneck ('I'd be buying both'), Arista Networks, and Marvell, which he has been buying for a while; Nokia is rejected as legacy telecom growing only 4-7%, and SpaceX is a wait given valuation and remaining lockup expirations despite its rebound to around IPO price. Tier 3: Broadcom, Marvell and Arista can all be owned together, and Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon are the safest cash-flow monsters that need no Nvidia cheque. Calls: BUY COHR, LITE, SNPS, MRVL, ANET, AVGO; AVOID INTC, NOK; HOLD SPCX; ORCL grouped with the weakest-link neoclouds but given no explicit stance in this video (UNCERTAIN; his prior tracked stance was AVOID). Captions garble several names — 'Cororeweave', Coherent's ticker as 'COR', Lumentum as 'Lummentum/LIT', Nokia as 'NK' — tickers above are the companies actually discussed; no share prices are stated in the video.

calls.thesis: First tracked INTC call — AVOID / pass for now: Nvidia's ~215M-share (~$30B, ~half its 13F portfolio) stake and the x86/AI partnership prop Intel up, but he is not convinced Intel Foundry can compete with TSMC in advanced manufacturing, which is what the stock depends on.

Reiterated HOLD / wait (prior HOLD): SpaceX could be a good long-term investment and has rebounded back around its IPO price, but he'd rather wait — valuation plus final lockup expirations coming off early investors over at least another month; Nvidia holds ~123M shares (~$21B) and SpaceX is reportedly seeking ~$40B largely to buy Nvidia chips.

First tracked COHR call — BUY: optical interconnect is 'quickly becoming the next bottleneck'; Nvidia holds 7.8M shares (~$3B) AND committed multi-billion-dollar purchases plus secured capacity rights — 'a stronger signal than just buying the stock... one I would definitely be following Nvidia into', and 'I'd be buying both of these' (COHR and LITE).

First tracked LITE call — BUY: Lumentum (captions render 'Lummentum, ticker LIT') received a separate ~$2B Nvidia investment and similar purchase commitments for optical technology moving data between AI processors; 'I'd be buying both of these as well' (with COHR).

Reiterated BUY: 'I do like this one' — Synopsys' chip-design software is critical to the industry, its business isn't dependent on Nvidia financing, the market isn't watching it as closely and valuation is still very good on ~37% expected revenue growth this year; Nvidia holds ~$2.1B.

First tracked NOK call — AVOID: despite Nvidia's ~$2.2B investment and the AI-in-telecom/6G partnership, Nokia is 'still too much of a legacy telecom company' and 4-7% expected annual revenue growth 'just doesn't offer the growth I'm looking for' in AI names.

Reiterated BUY: 'I've been buying Marvell now for a while' — one of the only competitors to Broadcom in custom AI accelerators; Nvidia's $2B investment + NVLink partnership brings a competitor into its own ecosystem, and he likes both sides of that opportunity.

First tracked ANET call — BUY: Arista Networks is 'another favorite' — networking hardware connecting massive AI data centers, a big Broadcom competitor where demand lets both win; 'I see no problem owning all three' (AVGO, MRVL, ANET).

Reiterated BUY: 'Broadcom is one of my favorites here' (tier 3 — benefits from Nvidia without depending on its financing); competes with MRVL in custom AI chips and also sells networking/other semis; he'd own AVGO, MRVL and ANET together.
